 Canadiens @ Maple Leafs: Game preview, start time, Tale of the Tape, and how to watch
 Top spot in the division is available to Montreal if it can beat its rival.
 Posted on November 7, 2026 November 7, 2026 by Justin Blades 
 Photo by Gerry Angus/Icon Sportswire 
 How to watch
 Game 17: Montreal Canadiens @ Toronto Maple Leafs
 Start time:  7:00 PM EST / 5:00 PM PDT 
In Canada: Sportsnet (English), TVA Sports (French)
Streaming: Sportsnet+, TVA Sports+ (Canada), ESPN+ (USA)
 The Toronto Maple Leafs had a hot stretch from October 19 to 24 that saw them outscore opponents 21-9 over a four-game winning streak that got a lot of people excited about how far the team can go this year. Since then they’ve settled back down to their early-season form of accumulating more losses than wins, and that’s about what was expected of them this season. They currently sit just outside the Eastern Conference’s second-wild spot, probably around where they will finish this season.
 A Leafs team that has seen quite a few changes from last season has scored 64 goals in 17 games while giving up an Atlantic Division-high 56. It’s high-event hockey being provided, although not as much in front of the home fans. They rank second in the league with 4.50 goals per game on the road, but are 22nd among home teams.
 Toronto’s possession numbers aren’t strong, slightly below average by just about any metric. A significant portion of Toronto’s offence is generated on its power play, which is currently operating at 25%. It’s not on the same level as the Utah Mammoth’s man advantage that went into Montreal ranked second in the league and scored three goals to vault to first, but it has scored 15 times in 17 games so far. The gameplan once again needs to be limiting the opponent’s power plays — or maybe having to go one step further and avoiding any contact that could be perceived as a penalty.

 This will be the Canadiens’ first intradivision game since October 17. That night they ran their record to 4-0 versus fellow teams in what is by far the most competitive section in the league. Every team holds at least a .500 points percentage, and the Canadiens are one of five teams north of .600. So far it’s just the three under that latter mark that Montreal has played. There is starting to be some separation, and Toronto and the Detroit Red Wings risk falling behind. The Habs will want to do their part to maintain that gap and reduce the number of teams competing for division spots at the end of the season.
 Montreal goes into the game with a chance to extend its point streak to double digits, one that started with that match versus Buffalo three weeks ago. Going into that night, the Canadiens were a .500 team themselves, not even in a wild-card spot. With a win tonight, they would catch the Boston Bruins at 25 points in the same number of games played, tying for the top spot in the Atlantic.
 A meeting with Boston next week could have that position on the line, but there is still a lot of work to do to get to that point, including what will be a very difficult matchup with the Minnesota Wild on Tuesday. Montreal first needs to focus on the game ahead of them because the Maple Leafs have the firepower to bite them if they look beyond this contest.
 The Canadiens are 5-1-1 on the road this year, second in the NHL just like they were a season ago. They tend to play their most stable game on the road, which is what they need versus a team heavily skewed toward offence.
